Ozerna Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Ternopil Oblast, Ukraine

Not demolished. Ozerna's cemetery holds a genuine discrepancy in the source record: one account states permanent Jewish settlement began only in the second half of the 19th century, when a Jew named Mandel Jampoler purchased an estate from Count Lubomirski and employed fellow Jews at a flour mill and distillery — yet epigraphic evidence shows this very cemetery already existed by 1851, meaning the community must have emerged earlier than that account suggests. In the 1870s, Jewish architects built the town's Great Synagogue, and the same architects also built two churches in Ozerna — a notable instance of interfaith professional collaboration. This cemetery is mentioned in the 1971 Yizkor memorial book Sefer Ozerna; according to local residents, it was severely damaged during WWII and finally destroyed in 1952.
